text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new ideas without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build a new function or fix a problem safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes and give feedback. This workflow keeps the code organized and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can work faster and more safely, because everyone can see what changed and why.
